canonical_examples.name:
Example: 
                    Listing the Terms of a Linear Expression
canonical_examples.problem: List all terms of the expression $3x + 2y - 4x.$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
We put an addition symbol $(+)$ between each part and separate using parentheses:

$$
(3x) + (2y) + (-4x)
$$

So, the expression has three terms: $3x$, $2y$, and $-4x.$

canonical_examples.name:
Example: 
                    Identifying Particular Terms of an Expression
canonical_examples.problem: What is the fourth term of the expression $2t + 5s - \dfrac{1}{2}s + 8t?$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
We put an addition symbol $(+)$ between each part and separate using parentheses:

$$
(2t) + (5s) + \left( -\dfrac{1}{2} s \right) + (8t)
$$

Counting off the terms:

- the first term is $2t,$

- the second term is $5s,$

- the third term is $-\dfrac{1}{2}s,$ and

- the fourth term is $8t.$

In particular, we are interested in the fourth term. The fourth term is $8t.$
canonical_examples.knowledge_point: Identifying Particular Terms of an Expression

canonical_examples.name:
Example: 
                    Equivalent Expressions
canonical_examples.problem: Write down an expression that is equivalent to $9-\dfrac{1}{2}x+3y.$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
The expression $9-\dfrac{1}{2}x+3y$ has three terms: $9,$ $-\dfrac{1}{2}x,$ and $3y.$

It doesn't matter in what order we write the terms. For example, one equivalent expression is:

$$
-\dfrac{1}{2}x + 3y +9
$$

Another equivalent expression is:

$$
3y - \dfrac{1}{2}x + 9
$$

tutorials.name: Introduction
tutorials.problem:
Let's take a look at the following algebraic expression:

$$
2x{\,\color{red}{-}\,} 4y {\,\color{blue}{+}\,} 7
$$

The addition $({\color{blue}{+}})$ and subtraction $({\color{red}{-}})$ symbols separate this expression into three parts known as **terms**.  

To identify each term, we put an addition symbol $({\color{blue}{+}})$ between each part and separate using parentheses:

$$
(2x) {\,\color{blue}{+}\,} ({\,\color{red}{-}\,} 4y) {\,\color{blue}{+}\,} (7).
$$

So, the terms of this expression are: 

$$
2x,\quad -4y,\quad  \quad 7
$$

We say that $2x$ is the **first term**, $-4y$ is the **second term**, and $7$ is the **third term**. 

In this example, the subtraction symbol gave us the term $-4y$. Whenever there is a subtraction symbol, the corresponding term will be negative.

tutorials.name: Equivalent Expressions
tutorials.problem:
When two algebraic expressions contain exactly the same terms, they are said to be **equivalent**.

For example, the expression

$$
{\color{blue}{x}} + {\color{red}{2y}} + 3z
$$

is equivalent to 

$$
3z+{\color{blue}{x}} + {\color{red}{2y}}
$$

because they both contain the exact same terms. Both expressions are also equivalent to

$$
{\color{blue}{x}} + 3z+ {\color{red}{2y}}.
$$
